questions.prompt:
Which of the following principles of divine morality does this verse refer to?
يوم تجد كل نفس ما عملت من خير محضرا وما عملت من سوء
questions.note: The photograph quotes the opening of Quran 3:30, describing the Day when each soul is confronted with its good and evil deeds. Thus B, belief in resurrection and accountability, is the most specific principle. Do not confuse it with the different verse about divine supervision in the separate Q3–12 fragment. First-term Lesson 1, p. 2 links resurrection to judgment of actions.

questions.prompt: According to Ibne Muskawiyyah, “kholq” is:
options: One of the traits of the human self which entices man to carry out his daily affairs without thinking.
One of the traits of the human self which entices man to carry out his daily affairs with thinking.
One of the traits of the human self which entices man to carry out his daily affairs with a lot of thought.
One of the traits of the human self which entices man to carry out his daily affairs without authority.
questions.note: Lesson 2, p. 3 describes an established disposition producing actions without fresh deliberation. It can become habitual through practice; the answer does not say that moral action must be mindless.

questions.note: The first-term definition includes internal moral qualities, good or bad, developed as character. All three descriptions fit Lesson 2; khulq is not the visible bodily form khalq.

questions.prompt: Which one is NOT true about the knowledge of ethics (science of Akhlaq)?
options: It identifies good and bad behaviors.
In the knowledge of ethics we study Khulq and Khalq.
It studies good and bad actions.
It deals with human characteristics and traits like vices and virtues.
questions.note: The course distinguishes moral character, khulq, from bodily creation, khalq. Its science-of-ethics definition studies moral traits and associated actions, not bodily creation as such. See first-term pp. 3–4.

questions.prompt: What does cultivation (tazkiye) mean?
options: Cultivation means restoring the human soul and nature to its original and natural purity and honesty.
Cultivation means doing a lot of worship.
Cultivation means serving the people and one’s family.
Cultivation means forgetting sins and doing new worship.
questions.note: This reproduces Lesson 3, question 2, p. 7. Cultivation concerns purification, rather than forgetting wrongs or simply accumulating acts.

questions.prompt: Why should believers not trust in any other person or thing apart from God?
options: A believer knows that this world belongs to God.
A believer knows that this world was created by God.
Everyone else is fully dependent on God.
All of the above are true.
questions.topic: Trust in God and responsible effort
questions.note: All three fit the course’s account of divine ownership and dependent causes. The stem concerns ultimate, independent reliance; using people, medicine and ordinary means remains compatible with trust. See the review pp. 5, 8 and 18.
questions.reviewNote: Trust includes responsible use of dependent natural means.
